subject.title: Feature request: config option to suppress transient tool error warnings

question: Should OpenClaw add a public normal-chat tool-error delivery policy beyond `messages.suppressToolErrors`, and what should happen when a mutating tool fails but the assistant final reply sounds successful?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the next change adds public config surface and changes safety behavior for failed side effects, so automation cannot choose the product contract safely.

options.title: Add opt-in delivery enum
options.body: Define a default-compatible enum such as `all | final | off` that preserves current warnings by default while allowing hosted/team-chat operators to opt into final-only or off behavior with focused tests.

options.title: Keep boolean-only policy
options.body: Treat `messages.suppressToolErrors` as the supported all-off escape hatch and document that OpenClaw does not infer success from final replies for failed side effects.

options.title: Move policy to channels
options.body: Let team-chat plugins own warning visibility where channel UX differs, avoiding another global message config key.

recommendation.title: Add opt-in delivery enum
recommendation.body: Define a default-compatible enum such as `all | final | off` that preserves current warnings by default while allowing hosted/team-chat operators to opt into final-only or off behavior with focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged warning-policy fix that explicitly left this broader config policy open and have the strongest relevant history in the inspected path.
